claim: Unmonitored 'wild goose chase' attempts (read, pick a direction, never reassess) are a main failure mode in human maths problem solving, and monitoring at junctures separates success from failure.
agent_test: Add a forced juncture check (every N steps ask: what am I doing, why, will it help) vs no check, equal tokens; count dead-end runs.

claim: Schoenfeld's 60% to 20% fall in wild-goose-chase behaviour after metacognitive questioning is second-hand (quoted by Rott 2013); the primary paper was not opened.
agent_test: Use as motivation only; do not cite the number as measured by us.

claim: Rott replicated the link in 45 fifth graders: wild-goose-chase processes reached advanced access in 5 of 32 (16%) vs 40 of 56 (71%) others; chi-square 25.378, p<0.0001. Caveat: the author's own operational definition and excluded cases make it partly circular.
agent_test: Label agent traces by the same rule and compare solve rate.

claim: Step-back (abstract to a principle first) gives large gains on knowledge-heavy tasks: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4 to 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 to 81.8, TimeQA 41.5 to 66.0; confirmed against the paper.
agent_test: Insert a step-back call before solving; compare with CoT at equal tokens on physics/knowledge items.

claim: Step-back gain shrinks with stronger models and is nil on GSM8K (84.3 vs CoT 84.4); on GPT-4 physics only +1.6 over CoT. Abstraction helps when the failure is a missing principle, not arithmetic.
agent_test: Gate step-back on item type; test that gating beats always-on.

claim: Step-back is net positive but not free: it fixes 20.5% of baseline errors and introduces 11.9% new ones (MMLU Physics); over 90% of remaining errors are reasoning, not principle, errors.
agent_test: Keep the original answer as a candidate and verify, rather than overwrite.

claim: Decomposing into easier subproblems (least-to-most) gives large gains on length generalisation (SCAN length split 99.7% vs CoT 16.2%; last-letter length 12: 74.0 vs 31.8) but small gains on GSM8K (+1.4 to +1.5 points).
agent_test: Compare decomposition vs flat CoT on long-chain vs short-chain items at equal tokens.

claim: Plan-first prompting (Plan-and-Solve) gives modest zero-shot gains: PS+ 76.7 vs zero-shot CoT 70.4 average on six arithmetic sets (text-davinci-003), GSM8K 59.3 vs 56.4; no better than 8-shot manual CoT (77.6). Evidence is on old models.
agent_test: Re-test on a current model; expect smaller gains.

claim: Plan-and-Solve error analysis (46 wrong GSM8K answers): calculation 7%, missing step 12%, semantic misunderstanding 27%. Record a19 gave 27% for missing step, which is wrong.
agent_test: None; bookkeeping correction.

claim: Self-generated analogous exemplars beat fixed few-shot CoT only slightly on GSM8K (75.0 to 77.8, GPT-3.5) and MATH (33.0 to 37.3); of 50 correct cases 35 had relevant correct exemplars, 9 relevant but wrong.
agent_test: Compare self-recalled analogues vs none; check that wrong-but-relevant exemplars do not hurt.

claim: Self-composed reasoning structures (Self-Discover) beat CoT on 21 of 25 tasks at 10-40x less compute than self-consistency, but on MATH the gain is 1-7 points and 74.7% of failures are computation errors, not structure errors.
agent_test: Choose the heuristic per item with one planning call; measure vs SC at equal tokens.

claim: Backward/reverse reasoning helps: RevThink +13.53% over student zero-shot (12 datasets, training-based); FOBAR backward verification beats self-consistency by 2.1 (davinci), 1.1 (GPT-3.5) and 0.3 (GPT-4) points. At GPT-4 level the gain is within noise, and with ComplexCoT SC (91.6) edges FOBAR-CoT. FOBAR adds backward chains on top of the same forward chains, so tokens are not matched; the matched-token comparison is still untested (d16).
agent_test: Add a backward check (plug answer back) vs an extra forward sample at equal tokens.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without an external signal does not help reasoning: GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9 to 74.7 after two rounds, GPT-4 95.5 to 89.0, CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1. Caveat from gap search: these are 2023 instruct models; R1-class models recover about 90% from planted errors in their own chain (d08), so the negative result does not carry to current long-CoT models.
agent_test: Do not add a free 'review your answer' loop; require a new check type (backward, tool, independent sample).

claim: Process-level checking beats outcome-level checking and voting: best-of-1860 on a MATH subset 78.2% (process reward) vs 72.4% (outcome) vs 69.6% (majority).
agent_test: Step-level verification vs final-answer verification at equal tokens.

claim: Models fail maths through brittleness, not method: GSM-Symbolic shows drops with changed numbers and up to 65% drop (Phi-3-mini) with one irrelevant clause (o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1, GPT-4o-mini -40.0); GSM-IC and premise-order studies agree (R-GSM GPT-4-turbo 94.1 to 85.0); GSM1k shows up to 8% contamination drop for some families. Update: brittleness persists in 2025 reasoning models (irrelevant sentence raises errors over 300% for R1, d13).
agent_test: Add a restate-and-strip-irrelevant step (specialise/understand) and test on distractor variants.

claim: Cognitive behaviours (verification, backtracking, subgoal setting, backward chaining) determine whether RL improves a model: primed Llama-3.2-3B matches Qwen-2.5-3B (about 30% to about 60% Countdown); length-matched empty CoT gives no gain; priming with incorrect solutions that keep the behaviours works about as well as correct. Single task (Countdown).
agent_test: Ablate each behaviour in the schema on one controlled task; Countdown-only limits transfer.

claim: On proof-based olympiad problems the strongest model scored 24.4% (USAMO 2025), others below 5%; failures include the same wrong strategy repeated across attempts, i.e. no strategy switching. Update: the opposite failure also exists in reasoning models (too many shallow switches: wrong answers use 418% more switches, d09). Neither pattern has been fixed by a tested intervention.
agent_test: Force strategy change after a failed attempt (specialise, work backward) and measure distinct strategies per item.

claim: Chain-of-thought gain concentrates on maths and symbolic tasks (up to 95% of MMLU gain on questions with '=').
agent_test: Apply the heavy schema only to maths/symbolic items; skip elsewhere.

claim: Human heuristic training: Schoenfeld 1979 (opened) is N=7, all 4 trained students beat all 3 controls (p=1/35). Rott and Gawlick 2014 replication (opened), N=28, explicit heuristic training beat practice-only with d=0.79 and no-training with d=1.44 (practice-only vs none d=0.64). Hembree 1992 and IMPROVE effect sizes remain unopened. Working-backward teaching in children (N=14) is uncontrolled.
agent_test: Treat human training as medium-to-large but from small samples; do not quote a pooled effect size.

claim: Forcing a plan-monitor-evaluate cycle on every query hurts a non-reasoning 8B model on GSM8K (Llama-3-8B: 80.71 standard, 69.55 with the forced cycle) and is neutral on a thinking 8B model (Qwen-3-8B: 91.72 vs 91.65); only a tiny seeded-error funnel (24 errors) shows better self-correction (50% vs 16%). No equal-token test exists.
agent_test: Fire the juncture monitor only on stall or at episode ends; compare with always-on and none at equal tokens; count dead-end runs.

claim: Generic 'think step by step' prompts add little on reasoning models: o3-mini +2.9, o4-mini +3.1, Gemini Flash 2.5 -3.3 points on GPQA Diamond at 20-80% more time; richer prompts (decompose, weigh paths) made no difference on GPT-4o. A scaffold must beat this bar at equal tokens.
agent_test: Benchmark every scaffold step against a bare reasoning-model run at matched tokens before keeping it.

claim: Specialise-then-conjecture works on answer-construction maths: enumerate small cases, conjecture a pattern, verify in Lean. Accuracy 14.54 to 45.06 (gpt-4.1-mini), 19.06 to 43.81 (deepseek-v3), also on post-cutoff problems (5.43 to 31.52). Untested on reasoning models, at equal tokens, or on proofs.
agent_test: Add a 'try n=1,2,3 and tabulate' operator on find-the-formula items; ablate against the same tokens spent on extra samples.

claim: Forced strategy switching has no direct evidence on proofs. Observed failures run both ways: same wrong strategy repeated (USAMO) and too many shallow switches (underthinking: +418% switches in wrong answers). A decode-time penalty on switching gave +0 to +6 points; a prompt to stay on one thought did not help R1 (72.4 vs 73.8).
agent_test: Switch rule: bounded depth on one approach, a stated failed check, then a different approach; log depth before each switch.

claim: Behaviour transfer: cognitive behaviours amplified by math-style pretraining show up far more often on GPQA (subgoal setting 6.5 vs 0.7 per question) but accuracy stays about 12%. No scaffolding-only test and no GSM8K or proof transfer test exists.
agent_test: Treat behaviour counts as a process check, not as evidence of better answers.

claim: Restate-and-strip works as an explicit step for older models: S2A regeneration raised GSM-IC from 51.7 to 61.3 (LLaMA-2-70B) while 'ignore irrelevant text' gave no consistent gain; but on Llama-3.1-8B an ignore instruction cut attack success 37.5% to 9.9%. Effect depends on model; few-shot examples did not fix GSM-NoOp.
agent_test: Test the restate-and-strip step against a plain 'ignore irrelevant' sentence on distractor variants, per model.

claim: More verification beats more voting at large budgets: Consistency@50 equals Consistency@10,000 on AIME while Verification@k keeps scaling (Gemini 1.5 Pro). FOBAR-style backward checks vs an extra sample at matched tokens is still untested.
agent_test: Spend a fixed budget on verification passes vs extra samples; report both.

claim: A forced 'Wait' re-check helps for a few repeats (AIME24 50 to 57% after up to 6) then causes loops; cap forced re-checks.
agent_test: Cap forced re-checks at a small number and stop on a loop signature.

claim: Per-item heuristic choice is untested. Self-Discover selects modules per task, with MATH gain of 2 to 5 points (GPT-4 71 to 73) and no ablation of individual Polya heuristics on one benchmark.
agent_test: Run a per-heuristic ablation (specialise, generalise, backward, analogy, decompose) on one set, with an oracle best-heuristic baseline.

claim: Problem-posing ('what if not') for frozen agents has no direct evidence; the nearest result is training-time self-proposed tasks (removing proposer training: 46.8 to 45.4 average).
agent_test: Only test if the agent gets open-ended tasks; low priority.

claim: Gap-search closure: gaps 4 (specialise) and 5 (human effect, partly) and 9 (restate step, older models) are mostly closed; gaps 1, 3, 6, 7, 8 are half-closed with indirect evidence; gaps 2 and 10 remain open; Hembree and IMPROVE effect sizes remain unread.
agent_test: Use as the index of what is tested vs untested.
